faq.question: What is Tangodachi?
faq.answer: Tangodachi is a free Japanese practice app for educators and learners. Educators create decks with AI, assign them with deadlines, and track how each learner is doing. Learners study with daily review, spaced repetition, practice games, and graded quizzes — more ways to make what they're learning stick. It works on any device — no install required.

faq.question: Is Tangodachi good for teachers?
faq.answer: Yes — it's designed for it. Teachers invite their whole group with a single QR code, assign specific decks with due dates, monitor each student's progress and accuracy, run graded quizzes with exportable results, and send encouragement messages. Tangodachi supplements what you already teach, giving students structured practice between lessons.

faq.question: Can students practice what they learn in class?
faq.answer: Yes. Once a teacher assigns a deck, students get daily review that resurfaces the words they need to see, plus practice modes and quick games built from those same words. It turns lesson vocabulary and grammar into short, repeatable practice students can do on their phone between lessons.

faq.question: What practice and review modes are available?
faq.answer: Every student gets a Daily Review, powered by spaced repetition, that surfaces the words due that day, plus three practice modes — Match (race the clock pairing words to meanings), Fill-in-the-blank (type the missing word in a sentence), and Recall (see the meaning, type the Japanese) — quick games, and graded quizzes. Every session earns XP toward the next level.

faq.question: How does AI flashcard generation work?
faq.answer: Teachers type any word in English or Japanese and Google Gemini generates the hiragana reading, kanji, meaning, and bilingual example sentences — so building course material takes minutes, not hours. You can also upload a PDF of a textbook or handout to extract vocabulary and generate cards in bulk.

faq.question: What is Travel Mode?
faq.answer: Travel Mode is a built-in pocket phrasebook with 9 interactive modules: Daily Phrases, Scenarios, Food Menu, Emergency, Listening Practice, Katakana Decoder, Culture Guide, Point & Communicate, and Show Cards. Each module prepares students for real conversations in Japan.

faq.question: Is Tangodachi free?
faq.answer: Tangodachi is currently free and in closed beta. Teachers and students can join the waitlist on the homepage to be notified when new spots open up.
